title: Adding Light and Dark Mode
summary: I added a button that lets users change the website between light mode and dark mode.
content: I wanted the website to have both a light and dark theme because many websites now give users this option. I used JavaScript to change the data-theme attribute on the page and used localStorage to remember the selected theme. The main challenge was that the theme button was inside the header, and the header was loaded later using JavaScript. I had to make sure the theme setup ran after the header was added to the page. This helped me understand how JavaScript, CSS, and localStorage can work together.

title: Loading the Header and Footer
summary: I created one shared header and footer that could be used on every page.
content: At first, I had the same navigation and footer code on each page. I realized that making a change would mean editing every page separately. I created header.html and footer.html files and used fetch in JavaScript to load them. One challenge was that the components would not load when I opened the HTML file directly from my computer. I learned that the website needed to run through a local server or GitHub Pages. This made the project easier to organize and update.

title: Loading Blog Posts from JSON
summary: I created a News page that loads all of its posts from a JSON file.
content: Instead of writing every blog post directly inside news.html, I stored the information in posts.json. JavaScript reads the file, sorts the posts by date, and creates a card for each one. I also added a Latest Post badge and a Read More button. I had trouble when the posts did not appear on my published website because some of the dates and content in the JSON file were incomplete. I corrected the JSON format and tested the file directly in the browser. This taught me that even a small mistake in JSON can stop the whole section from loading.

title: Validating the Contact Form
summary: I added validation to make sure users complete the contact form correctly.
content: I used JavaScript to check the form before showing the success message. The form checks that the name is entered, the email format is valid, and the message has at least 20 characters. The most difficult part was making each error message appear under the correct field and disappear when the user started correcting the information. I tested the form using empty fields, an incorrect email, and a short message. This helped me understand how to prevent a form from submitting until the information is valid.

title: Adding a Live Search Filter
summary: I added live search boxes to help users find products and news posts.
content: I added a search box to the Products page and another one to the News page. The JavaScript compares what the user types with the title, category, and description of each card. Cards that do not match are hidden, and a No Results Found message appears when nothing matches. The News page was more difficult because its cards are created after the JSON file loads. I had to make sure the filter started after the blog cards were added to the page. I learned more about selecting elements and changing what is displayed without reloading the page.

title: Finishing the Company Website
summary: I completed and tested the Volk Security Systems website and connected the project to my previous work experience.
content: I chose to create a security company website because I work at Window Guard and I previously helped create their website. That experience made this project more interesting to me because I was already familiar with security products and the type of information customers look for. For this project, I completed the Home, About, Services, Products, News, and Contact pages. I tested the navigation, theme button, blog posts, search filters, and contact form. One challenge was making sure all of the files were placed in the correct folders and that the links worked after publishing the website on GitHub Pages. I also checked that the website worked on smaller screens. This project helped me improve my understanding of how HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and JSON work together to create a complete website.
